_note: CALIBRATION ARM, criterion A2. At p = 1/2 the walker's drift is 1/2 whether
it stands on a particle or a hole, so the environment is invisible and this
recipe must reproduce experiments/01_srw's four exactly known constants:
gamma = 1/2, a0 = sqrt(2/pi) = 0.797885, omega1 = 1, a1 = -1/4. It will not
be bit-for-bit -- the environment consumes its own randomness -- so the
test is distributional plus agreement of the fitted constants inside their
standard errors. This is what catches a wrong update order, a drift, or a
broken window boundary before any of it is blamed on physics.
The "snr" rule with NO omega1 states no design constant at all: the
uninformed default 0 makes n_i flat, which was measured on srw to be the
best of five arms for identifying omega1 (see
models/rwre.py's cost_hint supplies it, and the pilot measures it from the
clock and only scores the declaration against it.
